senses.gloss:
मुर् 1. मुर्, ऊर्, Ved. (fr. rt. मृ), a mortal,
(Sāy. = मरण-स्वभाव, मरण-शील.)

मुर् 2. मुर्, ऊर्, f. (fr. rt. मुर्छ्), fainting;
see Scholiast on Pāṇ. VI. 4, 21.

मुर् 3. मुर्, ऊर् (fr. rt. मुर्व्), binding,
tying.

मुर् 4. मुर्, cl. 6. P. मुरति, &c., to en-
compass, surround, encircle, entwine, bind
together; [cf. perhaps Lat. murus.]
5. मुर्, ऊर्, Ved. a wall (?).

मुर, अस्, m., N. of a Daitya slain by Kṛṣṇa;
(आ), f. a species of fragrant plant (named after the
Daitya); said to be the N. of the wife of Nanda
and mother of Candra-gupta; (अम्), n. encompass-
ing, surrounding.
—मुर-जित्, त्, m. ‘conqueror of
Mura,’ epithet of Kṛṣṇa or Viṣṇu.
—मुर-द,
अस्, m. ‘Mura-cutting,’ the discus of Viṣṇu.
—मुर-
द्विष्, ट्, m. ‘foe of Mura,’ epithet of Kṛṣṇa or
Viṣṇu.
—मुर-भिद्, त्, m. ‘cleaver of Mura,’ epi-
thet of Kṛṣṇa or Viṣṇu.
—मुर-मर्दन, अस्,
m. ‘crusher of Mura,’ epithet of Kṛṣṇa or Viṣṇu.
—मुर-रिपु, उस्, m. ‘enemy of Mura,’ epithet of
Kṛṣṇa or Viṣṇu.
—मुर-वैरिन्, ई, m. ‘enemy
of Mura,’ epithet of Kṛṣṇa or Viṣṇu.
—मुर-
हन्, हा, m. ‘slayer of Mura,’ epithet of Kṛṣṇa or
Viṣṇu.
—मुरारि (˚र-अरि), इस्, m. ‘enemy of
Mura,’ epithet of Kṛṣṇa or Viṣṇu; N. of the
author of the Murāri-nāṭaka or Anargha-rāghava;
N. of a commentary on the Kātantra grammar.
—मुरारि-गुप्त, अस्, m., N. of a pupil of Caitanya.
—मुरारि-नाटक, अम्, n., N. of a drama by Mu-
rāri, = Anargha-rāghava.
—मुरारि-भट्ट, अस्, m.,
N. of a teacher.
—मुरारि-मिश्र, अस्, m., N. of a
scholar, = Murāri (author of the Murāri-nāṭaka).
—मुरारि-विजय, अस्, m., N. of a drama.

मूर 1. मूर, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. = मूढ,
stupefied, bewildered, stupid, dull, foolish; [cf. अ-म्˚,
अ-प्रम्˚.]

मूर 2. मूर, अस्, आ, अम् (perhaps fr. a form
मू = rt. 1. मीव्), Ved. rushing, impetuous; (accord-
ing to Sāy.) destroying killing (= मारक, fr. rt.
मृ).
—मूर-देव, अस्, m., Ved. epithet of a par-
ticular kind of demon; (Sāy.) sporting in destruction
(= मारण-क्रीड).
मूर 3. मूर, अम्, n., Ved. = मूल, a root.

मुरगण्ड मुरगण्ड, अस्, m. an eruption on
the face (= वरण्ड).
मुरङ्गी मुरङ्गी. See मुरुङ्गी, col. 3.

मुरचीपत्तन मुरची-पत्तन, N. of a town
in the Dekhan, (also read मरीचि-पत्तन.)

मुरज मुरज, अस्, m. (thought by some to
be a comp. of मुर + ज), a kind of drum, tam-
bourine; a Śloka artificially arranged in the form of
a drum; (आ), f. a great drum; N. of Kuvera's wife.
—मुरज-फल, अस्, m. the jack fruit tree, Arto-
carpus Integrifolia.
मुरजक, अस्, m., N. of one of Śiva's attendants.

मुरण्ड मुरण्ड, अस्, m. a country to the
[]
north-west of Hindūstān (called also Lampāka, and
now Lamghan in Cabul); (आस्), m. pl., N. of a
people; [cf. मुरुण्ड.]

मुरन्दला मुरन्दला, f., N. of a river (=
मुरला; thought by some to be Narma-dā).

मुरमण्ड मुरमण्ड (probably incorrect)
for मुरगण्ड, q. v.

मुरल मुरल, अस्, m. (probably fr. rt. 4.
मुर्), a species of fresh-water fish; a king of the
Muralas; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people; (आ), f., N.
of a river in the country of the Keralas, = मुरन्-
दला, q. v.; (ई), f. a flute, pipe.
—मुरली-धर,
अस्, m. ‘flute-bearer,’ an epithet of Kṛṣṇa.
मुरलिका, f., N. of a woman.

मुरवार मुरवार, अस्, m., N. of a king of
the Turuṣkas.

मुरसिदाबाद मुरसिदाबाद, N. of a city
(مرشد آباد).
मुराद मुराद, अस्, m. a proper N.

मुरु मुरु, उस्, m., N. of a country; N. of
a Daitya slain by Kṛṣṇa [cf. मुर]; (said to be)
a species of plant (in explanation of मौर्वी); a kind
of iron.
—मुरु-देश, अस्, m., N. of a country; [cf.
मरु-देश.]
मूरु मूरु, N. of a country.

मुरुङ्गी मुरुङ्गी, f. Moringa Pterygos-
perma, (also spelt मुरङ्गी.)
मुरुण्डक, अस्, m., N. of a mountain in Udyāna.

मुरुताणदेश मुरुताण-देश, अस्, m., N. of
a country.

मुर्छ् मुर्छ्, cl. 1. P. मूर्छति, मुमूर्छ,
मूर्छिष्यति, अमूर्छीत्, मूर्छितुम्,
to settle into a fixed or solid form, assume definite
shape or substance, acquire consistency; to congeal,
become dense, thicken, coagulate, stiffen; to become
torpid or stupefied, become senseless, lose conscious-
ness, faint away, swoon, be troubled in mind; to be
infatuated; to increase, grow, become strong, gather
strength, become stronger or more intense, acquire
vehemence or power, be powerful or effectual, take
effect, (मारुतस्य रंहः शिलोच्छये न मूर्-
छति, the velocity of the wind has no power against
a mountain); to be a match for; to be frequent;
to fill, penetrate, pervade; to make to sound loudly,
play loudly: Caus. मूर्छयति, -यितुम्, to cause to
settle into a fixed or solid form, give form to, form
(Ved.); to congeal, curdle (Ved.); to stupefy, cause
to faint, make senseless; to strengthen, augment;
to excite; to cause to sound loudly, play (a musical
instrument).

मूर्ख, अस्, आ, अम्, stupid, foolish, silly, igno-
rant, dull, unintelligent; inexperienced in (with loc.);
(अस्), m. a fool, blockhead; a sort of bean, Phaseolus
Radiatus.
—मूर्ख-ता, f. or मूर्ख-त्व or
मूर्ख-भूय, अम्, n. stupidity, folly, foolishness,
dulness.
—मूर्ख-भ्रातृक, अस्, m. one who has
a foolish brother.
—मूर्ख-मण्डल, अम्, n. a
collection or assemblage of fools.
—मूर्ख-व्यसनि-
नायक, अस्, आ, अम्, having a foolish and vicious
commander.
—मूर्ख-शत, अम्, n. a hundred fools.
—मूर्खी-भू, cl. 1. P. -भवति, -भवितुम्, to
become stupid or foolish.
मूर्ख मूर्ख. See P. 785, col. 3.

मूर्खिमन्, आ, m. dulness, stupidity, folly (=
मूर्ख-ता).

मूर्छत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, becoming senseless, faint-
ing, swooning.

मूर्छन, अस्, ई, अम्, stupefying, causing insen-
sibility (applied to one of the five arrows of Kāma-
deva or Cupid); strengthening, augmenting, con-
firming; (अम्, आ), n. f. fainting, swooning, syncope;
vehemence, violence, prevalence, growth, increase,
(in this sense usually अम्, n.); swelling or rising of
[]
sounds, an intonation, note, a tone or semitone in
the musical scale, the seventh part of a Grāma or
scale, (each Grāma or scale consisted of seven notes
and contained also seven Mūrchanās); modulation,
melody, (in these senses usually आ, f.); a particular
process in metallic preparations, calcining quicksilver
with sulphur, (in this sense only अम्, n.)
मूर्छन मूर्छन. See p. 785, col. 3.

मूर्छा, f. fainting, loss of consciousness, a swoon,
stupor; spiritual stupor or blindness, delusion, hallu-
cination; the rising of sounds, diatonic scale; a par-
ticular process in calcining metals.
—मूर्छाक्षेप
(˚छा-आक्˚), अस्, m. (in rhetoric) expressing vehement
dissent or disapprobation by fainting.
—मूर्छा-
परीत, अस्, आ, अम्, overcome with faintness or
swooning, fainting away, insensible, (according to a
Scholiast = निश्चेतन.)
—मूर्छा-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्,
suffering from faintness, swooning away.

मूर्छाल, अस्, आ, अम्, fainting, fainted, swooning,
insensible.

मूर्छित, अस्, आ, अम्, stupefied, rendered sense-
less, fainted, fainting, insensible, bewildered, infatu-
ated; intoxicated; stupid, ignorant; rendered vehe-
ment or violent, intensified; grown, increased, aug-
mented, swollen; rising upwards, lofty; filled with;
calcined (as quicksilver; cf. मूर्छन); (अम्), n.
epithet of a kind of song or air.

मूर्त, अस्, आ, अम्, thickened, congealed, coagu-
lated, curdled (Ved.); settled into any fixed shape,
formed, substantial, solid, material, corporeal, em-
bodied, incarnate; real (said of the practically useful
division of time as opposed to the अ-मूर्त, the
unreal or imaginary division); stupefied, unconscious,
fainted, insensible.
—मूर्त-त्व, अम्, n. the posses-
sion of a form, embodiment, corporality, incarnate
existence, materiality.
—मूर्त-मात्र, अम्, n. that
which is merely material, only corporeal.
मूर्त मूर्त, मूर्ति. See p. 786, col. 1.

मूर्ति, इस्, f. (often written मूर्त्ति), any solid
body, any tangible or material form, (in philosophy)
anything which has definite shape and limits (as
earth, air, fire, water, and mind, but not आकाश,
ether), a material element (especially as a component
part of the human body), body, form, visible shape,
matter, substance; embodiment, manifestation, in-
carnation, personification, (मूर्तिर् धर्मस्य शाश्-
वती, an eternal personification of justice; cf. तपो-
म्˚); an image, statue, figure, form; beauty; N.
of the first astrological house; N. of a daughter of
Dakṣa and wife of Dharma; (इस्), m., N. of one
of the sages under the tenth Manu; [cf. perhaps Gr.
βρέτας, μορφή.]
—मूर्ति-तस्, ind. from the form,
bodily, substantially.
—मूर्ति-त्व, अम्, n. the being
or having a body, corporeity, embodiment, materiality,
(मूर्तित्वे परिकल्पितः, made into bodily shape.)
—मूर्ति-धर, अस्, आ, अम्, having a body, em-
bodied, corporeal, incarnate.
—मूर्ति-प, अस्, m.
‘image-keeper,’ a priest who guards an idol.
—मूर्ति-
भाव, अस्, m. the state of assuming a solid form,
corporeity.
—मूर्ति-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having a
material or bodily form, material, embodied, corpo-
real, incarnate, personified [cf. ख-म्˚, विश्व-म्˚];
(आन्), m., N. of a son of Kuśa; (अत्), n. a body.
—मूर्ति-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, possessing a particular
form.
—मूर्ति-मात्रा, f. a particle of matter.
—मूर्ति-लिङ्ग, perhaps = Prāg-jyotiṣa, the city of
Naraka.

मुर्भिणी मुर्भिणी, f. a chafing-dish, small
fire-place, fire-pan.

मुर्मुर मुर्मुर, अस्, m. (an onomatopoetic
word), a fire made of chaff, burning chaff; the god
of love; N. of one of the horses of the sun; (आ),
f., N. of a river.

मुर्व् मुर्व् [cf. rt. 1. मू], cl. 1. P. मूर्वति,
मूर्वितुम्, to bind, tie; [cf. मूर्वा.]

मूर्खलिका मूर्खलिका, f. an arrow in the
form of a bird's heart.
मूर्ण मूर्ण. See under rt. मॄ, p. 793.

मूर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, crushed, broken; = 2. मूत,
bound; [cf. rt. मुर्व्.]

मूर्धन् मूर्धन्, आ, m. (in Uṇādi-s. 1. 158.
said to be fr. rt. मुर्व्, to bind), the forehead, brow,
skull; the head in general; a head, chief, leader,
superior, (सर्वेषाम् भूतानाम् मूर्धा राजा, the
king is the head of all creatures); the highest or
foremost or most prominent part, surface, top, point,
peak, summit, (पर्वतस्य मूर्धा, the top or
peak of a mountain); ‘the summit,’ epithet of a
particular spiritual condition with Buddhists; (in
geometry) the base, (opposed to अग्र); मूर्ध्नि
or मूर्धनि, at the head or highest point, at the
beginning or commencement, in the front, (अतिष्-
ठन् मनुजेन्द्राणाम् मूर्ध्नि, he stood at the
head of the kings of men; सङ्ग्राम-मूर्धनि,
in the front of the battle); before, above, over.
—मूर्ध-कर्णी or मूर्ध-कर्परी, f. or मूर्-
ध-खोल, अम्, n. a broad-brimmed hat (worn as
a shelter from rain); an umbrella.
—मूर्ध-ज,
अस्, m. ‘head-born,’ the hair of the head, (in this
sense usually आस्, m. pl.); the mane; N. of a king (a
Cakra-vartin).
—मूर्धज-राग, अस्, m. colouring
or dyeing the hair.
—मूर्ध-ज्योतिस्, इस्, n. = ब्रह्म-
रन्ध्र, q. v.
—मूर्ध-तस्, ind., Ved. upon the
head.
—मूर्ध-तैलिक, अस्, m., with वस्ति, epithet
of a kind of Errhine for the head.
—मूर्धन्-वत्,
आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. containing the word मूर्धन्;
(आन्), m., N. of a Gandharva; of an Āṅgirasa or
Vāma-devya, author of the hymn Ṛg-veda X. 88.
—मूर्ध-पात, अस्, m. the splitting of the skull.
—मूर्ध-पिण्ड, अस्, m. a lump upon the head
(of an elephant in rut).
—मूर्ध-पुष्प, अस्, m.
the tree Mimosa Sirissa (शिरीष).
—मूर्ध-रस,
अस्, m. the scum of boiled rice, rice-water.
—मूर्-
ध-वेष्टन, अम्, n. a turban, fillet, diadem.
—मूर्धान्त (˚ध-अन्˚), अस्, m. the crown of
the head.
—मूर्धाभिषिक्त (˚ध-अभ्˚), अस्, आ,
अम्, having the head sprinkled, anointed, inaugu-
rated, consecrated, installed; (अस्), m. a consecrated
king; a man of the Kṣatriya or warrior caste; a
royal counsellor, minister; = मूर्धावसिक्त below.
—मूर्धाभिषेक (˚ध-अभ्˚), अस्, m. ‘head-
sprinkling,’ the act of consecrating any one (as king),
anointing, inaugurating.
—मूर्धावसिक्त (˚ध-
अव्˚), अस्, m. epithet of a particular mixed caste, the
[]
son of a Brāhman father by a Kṣatriya mother; =
मूर्धाभिषिक्त, a consecrated king.

मूर्ध = मूर्धन् (at the end of certain comps.,
cf. द्वि-म्˚, त्रि-म्˚).
मूर्धक, अस्, m. a Kṣatriya.

मूर्धन्य, अस्, आ, अम्, being on or in the head,
belonging to the head, capital; coming from the
head or skull, cerebral (a term applied to a class of
letters representing sounds formed high in the mouth
or by keeping back the tip of the tongue as far as
possible in the head and slightly turning it upwards,
e. g. ऋ, ॠ, ट्, ठ्, ड्, ढ्, ण्, र्, ष्; these letters are
sometimes called linguals); uppermost, highest, su-
perior, pre-eminent; (आ), f., N. of the mother of
Veda-śiras.
मूर्ध्वन्, आ, m. = मूर्धन्.

मूर्वा मूर्वा, f. (according to some also
मूर्वी, f.; probably fr. rt. मुर्व्), Sanseviera Rox-
burghiana, a sort of creeper from the fibres of which
bow-strings and the girdle of the Kṣatriyas are made,
a sort of hemp for bow-strings; [cf. मौर्व.]
—मूर्वा-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, made of Mūrvā.
मूर्विका, f. = मूर्वा.
